bull.b: Growing prescriptions, prescriber count, and refill rates indicate expanding physician adoption and patient persistence for Emrosi. This supports a more durable commercial base, improves the opportunity to scale revenue, and may strengthen the product’s position in rosacea treatment over the next several quarters.

Additional national formulary access can shift prescriptions from bridging programs toward reimbursed sales, supporting higher average selling prices and improved gross-to-net economics. Broader coverage also reduces access friction and creates a structural pathway for continued Emrosi penetration.

Positive EBITDA for consecutive quarters, alongside faster growth in product sales than expenses, indicates improving operating leverage as Emrosi scales. If sustained, this trend can support reinvestment in commercial expansion while moving the business closer to consistent profitability.

bear.b: Negative EBIT means reported net income does not yet reflect stable core operating profitability. The gap between earnings and operating performance raises durability concerns, because future results may depend on non-recurring or non-operating items rather than repeatable commercial economics.

The strong TTM cash result has not yet been demonstrated across a sustained history, with negative annual cash flow in every period from 2021 through 2025. This volatility makes internal funding capacity less predictable and increases the risk that future growth requires additional financing.

Emrosi’s commercial progress still depends on converting coverage into broader formulary placement, while bridging support remains important for some patients. Delays in access expansion could limit reimbursed volume, constrain pricing and gross-to-net improvement, and make growth more execution-sensitive.
